items.title: Firefox 159 patches 167 security holes and adds website watch feature — free at firefox.com
items.summary: Mozilla released Firefox 159 on October 28, 2026 addressing 167 vulnerabilities (108 high severity) and enabling the sidebar password manager by default. The new Smart Window feature watches websites for changes like price drops or new content. Get it free at firefox.com or via Firefox menu > Help > About Firefox.

items.title: Clearwave Fiber and Xfinity expand service to 3300 Columbia County addresses — check yours at clearwavefiber.com
items.summary: Clearwave Fiber has expanded its all-fiber infrastructure in Lake City with several thousand residents now able to get fiber internet. Xfinity and Comcast Business also announced high-speed service for 3,300+ homes and businesses in Columbia County. Check your address at clearwavefiber.com or xfinity.com to see if service reached your street.

items.title: Windows 11 24H2 Home Pro editions reached final security update October 13 — KB5127648 is the last one
items.summary: Microsoft confirmed Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro editions reached end of servicing on October 13, 2026. The October Patch Tuesday update KB5127648 is the final monthly security update these editions will receive. No further security patches after this. Check your edition at Settings > System > About and plan your next steps.

items.title: Run private AI chatbots on your computer free offline — Ollama LM Studio Jan GPT4All compared
items.summary: Want ChatGPT-like AI without the cloud? Four free tools let you run models locally: Ollama (command line, ollama.com), LM Studio (graphical, lmstudio.ai), Jan (chat interface, jan.ai), and GPT4All (simple desktop app, gpt4all.io). All work offline, no account needed, your data never leaves your computer. Download any from their official sites.

items.title: Chrome's 7th Zero-Day This Year Is Actively Exploited — Update Now
items.summary:
Google just patched Chrome's seventh actively exploited zero-day of 2026.
That's seven times this year that attackers found a hole in Chrome
before Google did — and used it against real people.

The flaw (vulnerability) lives in Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine.
Visit a malicious website and the code runs on your computer — no
clicks, no downloads, just loading the page. Google confirmed active
exploitation. CISA added it to their "must-patch-now" list.

items.title: CISA adds critical PHP flaws to exploited list — patch now at php.net
items.summary: CISA added two PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26. Attackers are actively using these "php2shell" flaws for remote code execution. If you run a website or server with PHP, update to the latest PHP version immediately at php.net/downloads.

items.title: **Headline:** Microsoft Edge 156 patches security holes — update free at edge://settings/help
items.summary: Microsoft released Edge 156 on October 22 (main release) and 156.0.4314.50 on October 26 with security fixes. Open Edge, click the three-dot menu → Help and feedback → About Microsoft Edge. It checks and installs updates automatically. Restart when prompted.

items.title: Outdated Software Is an Open Door — Here Is What to Update Now
items.summary: Outdated software is the open door attackers walk through. Old versions of Adobe Reader, Java, browser plugins, and utility tools have known holes that automated scripts scan for constantly. You don't need to be targeted — just running an old version is enough.

items.title: Firefox 158 gets a fresh Nova look and brings back Compact Mode — free update at firefox.com
items.summary: Update Firefox to version 158 at firefox.com or click Menu > Help > About Firefox. The Nova redesign refreshes tabs and toolbars with a cleaner look, and Compact Mode returns to fit more on screen — just right-click the toolbar and choose Customize Toolbar > Density > Compact.
